ticks.note: KIELER netlist bug. The entry action runs in every tick (tick 1 enters A, then the self-loop re-enters it in every tick), so shown should equal count: 1, 2, 3, ... (the priority-based compiler does: see the -priority twin). The netlist optimiser treats count += 1 as if it were count = 1 when it propagates constants through code that runs unconditionally, so shown = 1 for ever. Tick 1: count = 1, shown = 1.

kielerBug: Netlist PartialAssignmentEvaluation ignores the assignment operator: after x += c in unconditional code it assumes x == c. Intended (priority) result: shown = count = 1, 2, 3.
